title: Develop continuous model-market watch operational runbook and signal cadence
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build an operational runbook, signal taxonomy, and daily/weekly cadence for continuous monitoring of the open-model and vendor landscape so PM, procurement, and runtime teams can detect supply & capability regressions early and trigger predefined responses.

Scope:
- Define signal taxonomy (availability, latency delta, quantization compatibility, model quality drift against Redwood evals, license & pricing changes, region availability, outage frequency).
- Specify ingestion sources: vendor status pages, GitHub releases, model hub metadata, partner emails, cloud region announcements, telemetry from Redwood runtime (latency/failed-infers), support incident tags.
- Create scoring model for signal prioritization (severity, coverage, customer impact, speed of remediation).
- Define cadence and artifacts: daily digest (ops-facing), weekly watchlist (PM & sales-facing), quarterly market summary (exec).
- Document automated alerts, escalation path, and fallback runbooks (e.g., model substitution, traffic routing to fallback region or model variant).
- Deliverables: runbook doc, Confluence playbooks, Kibana/Grafana watch dashboards, template Slack alerts, initial vendor-prioritization matrix.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Runbook doc published in Confluence with owner and on-call rotations.
2) Signal ingestion pipeline produces first-week digest and watchlist for two model families.
3) Dashboards show at least three signal streams (availability, p95 latency delta, quantization-compatibility errors).
4) Two fallback playbooks (regional reroute, model-variant fallback) validated by a tabletop exercise.

Notes on approach and trade-offs:
- We will prioritize telemetry-first signals (latency, error rates) for high-fidelity early detection, accepting that external signals (license changes, vendor announcements) will be noisier and require manual enrichment.
- Initial scoring will favor customer-impact heuristics (active contract exposure, high-volume routes) over purely technical severity to align procurement and sales.
- To minimize engineering lift upfront, the first iteration will combine lightweight scrapers + manual enrichment; automation of scrapers and normalization is planned in cycle 2025-W14.

Stakeholders: Product (Aisha, Miguel), Runtime Eng (lead: Priya Rao), Observability (lead: Ben Cho), Solutions/Sales (lead: Nina Fischer), Legal/Procurement (review: Daniel Liu).
